mission_1.search: On the open map, BFS and A* both found a path of 13.5 m, so the lengths are equal. A* examined fewer cells: it expanded 700, while BFS expanded 928. My BFS uses a queue, which removes the oldest cell first, so it spreads out evenly in every direction, including away from the goal. My A* uses a heap ordered by cost so far plus the heuristic, so cells that look closer to the goal come out first, and many cells behind the start are never expanded. It still finds a shortest path because the Manhattan distance never overestimates the true distance.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, DFS found a much longer path than BFS, 104 m against 24.5 m, because my DFS uses a stack and follows the newest branch deep into the maze, returning the first route it reaches, while BFS uses a queue and explores by distance. IDDFS ended in resource_limit after 250,001 expansions because it restarts at depth 0 for every limit and repeats the same cells each pass. On the unreachable map, all four planners (BFS, DFS, IDDFS and A*) returned no_path. no_path means the search checked every reachable cell and found no route, while resource_limit means the runner stopped the search at its budget, so it says nothing about whether a path exists. I used AI to help write the planners, then read through each one to understand it myself and checked the results myself: BFS and A* matched in path length, DFS was longer than optimal, and all four agreed on no_path.
